changes._why: revenue counted cancelled and refunded orders, unlike CO_SCHEMA_I_02 (Claude); a store with no line was dropped and tied stores made the running total unstable (Codex)
request: The regional manager wants each store's revenue from completed orders, `0` for a store with none, its rank, its share of the chain's total, and a running total from the best store down; stores with the same revenue are ordered by `store_id`.
changes.sql:
WITH revenues AS (SELECT s.store_id, s.store_name, COALESCE(SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity), 0) AS revenue
                  FROM stores s
                           LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id AND o.order_status = 'COMPLETE'
                           LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
                  GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name)
SELECT store_id,
       store_name,
       revenue,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC)                                          AS revenue_rank,
       ROUND(100 * revenue / NULLIF(SUM(revenue) OVER (), 0), 2)                   AS share_pct,
       SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC, store_id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS running_total
FROM revenues
ORDER BY revenue DESC, store_id

changes._why: an address with nothing before an @, or no @, made SUBSTR NULL, so exactly the worst ones were hidden
request: Accounts are meant to be opened as `first.last@...`.

Data quality wants the customers whose email address, before the `@`, is not their full name in lower case with the spaces turned into dots, including the addresses with nothing before an `@` or no `@` at all; customers with the same name are ordered by `customer_id`.
changes.sql:
SELECT customer_id, full_name, email_address
FROM customers
WHERE INSTR(email_address, '@') <= 1
   OR SUBSTR(email_address, 1, INSTR(email_address, '@') - 1) <> LOWER(REPLACE(full_name, ' ', '.'))
ORDER BY full_name, customer_id

changes._why: LAG over order_tms alone: two orders at one moment could each be the other's previous; order_id breaks the tie, as CO_ORDERS_A_03 does
request: Customer care, looking at one customer, wants each of their orders next to the one before it, and the whole days between the two, to see how often they come back; orders placed at the same moment are ordered by `order_id`.
changes.sql:
SELECT order_id,
       order_tms,
       previous_order_tms,
       EXTRACT(DAY FROM order_tms - previous_order_tms) AS days_since_previous
FROM (SELECT order_id, order_tms, LAG(order_tms) OVER (ORDER BY order_tms, order_id) AS previous_order_tms
      FROM orders
      WHERE customer_id = :customerId)
ORDER BY order_tms, order_id

changes._why: the year's start came from SYSDATE, the host's clock, and now from LOCALTIMESTAMP, the session's; around New Year they disagree
request: Finance wants the number and value of the orders placed since the start of the current year, by month.
The start of the year and now are both taken from `LOCALTIMESTAMP`, one clock, as the JPQL takes them from one `:yearStart` and `LOCAL DATETIME`.
changes.sql:
SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_tms)  AS order_month,
       COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)        AS orders,
       SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity)  AS revenue
FROM orders o
         JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_tms >= TRUNC(LOCALTIMESTAMP, 'YYYY')
  AND o.order_tms < LOCALTIMESTAMP
GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_tms)
ORDER BY order_month

changes._why: a cancelled or refunded order never ships, so its unassigned lines were work that does not exist
request: Logistics wants the orders, other than cancelled or refunded ones, that still have lines with no shipment assigned, and how many such lines each has, the most first; orders with the same number are ordered by `order_id`.
changes.sql:
SELECT o.order_id, o.order_status, COUNT(*) AS unshipped_lines
FROM orders o
         JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE oi.shipment_id IS NULL
  AND o.order_status NOT IN ('CANCELLED', 'REFUNDED')
GROUP BY o.order_id, o.order_status
ORDER BY unshipped_lines DESC, o.order_id

changes._why: the note admitted the order was unstable among stores with the same stock but left it so; SELECT * brought the known product along
request: A merchandiser wants every store's stock of a product, lowest first, to see which stores need it replenished first; stores with the same stock are ordered by `store_id`.
changes.sql:
SELECT store_id, product_inventory
FROM inventory
WHERE product_id = :productId
ORDER BY product_inventory, store_id

changes._why: SUBSTR(name, -4) is NULL in Oracle for a name shorter than 4 characters, while the JPQL RIGHT(name, 4) gives the whole name
request: The signage team needs store names without spaces, for file names: `New York City` becomes `New-York-City`, and the last four characters of each, the whole name if it is shorter, are used as a short code.
changes.sql:
SELECT store_name,
       REPLACE(store_name, ' ', '-')                       AS slug,
       UPPER(SUBSTR(store_name, -LEAST(4, LENGTH(store_name)))) AS short_code
FROM stores
ORDER BY store_name

changes._why: it asked two questions, and its second, list price above every price sold at, is a narrower CO_SCHEMA_I_05
request: Finance wants the orders containing at least one line charged above `:price` per unit.
changes.sql:
SELECT o.order_id, o.order_tms
FROM orders o
WHERE :price < ANY (SELECT oi.unit_price FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.order_id = o.order_id)
ORDER BY o.order_id

changes._why: a distance in degrees of latitude and longitude can pick the wrong neighbour; the great-circle distance, with ties
request: For each store with both coordinates, show its nearest other store with both coordinates, all of them at a tie, and the great-circle distance in kilometres.
changes.sql:
WITH distances AS (SELECT s.store_id,
                          s.store_name,
                          n.store_name AS nearest_store,
                          6371 * ACOS(GREATEST(-1, LEAST(1,
                              SIN(s.latitude * ACOS(-1) / 180) * SIN(n.latitude * ACOS(-1) / 180)
                              + COS(s.latitude * ACOS(-1) / 180) * COS(n.latitude * ACOS(-1) / 180)
                                * COS((s.longitude - n.longitude) * ACOS(-1) / 180)))) AS km
                   FROM stores s
                            JOIN stores n ON n.store_id <> s.store_id
                   WHERE s.latitude IS NOT NULL
                     AND s.longitude IS NOT NULL
                     AND n.latitude IS NOT NULL
                     AND n.longitude IS NOT NULL)
SELECT store_name, nearest_store, ROUND(km, 2) AS km
FROM (SELECT d.*, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY store_id ORDER BY km) AS rnk FROM distances d)
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY store_name, nearest_store

changes._why: it ranked the rounded kilometres, so a farther donor could win, with no tie-break on equal distance or surplus; the ACOS argument unclamped
request: With `0 <= :minStock <= :targetStock`, for each stocked product below `:minStock` at a store, propose the nearest store above `:targetStock` as the donor, the larger surplus and then the lower `store_id` at a tie, and a donor with no distance only as a fallback; propose no more than the need or the surplus.
changes.sql:
WITH short AS (SELECT store_id, product_id, :targetStock - product_inventory AS need
               FROM inventory
               WHERE product_inventory < :minStock),
     spare AS (SELECT store_id, product_id, product_inventory - :targetStock AS surplus
               FROM inventory
               WHERE product_inventory > :targetStock),
     pairs AS (SELECT sh.store_id AS to_store_id,
                      sp.store_id AS from_store_id,
                      sh.product_id,
                      sh.need,
                      sp.surplus,
                      6371 * ACOS(GREATEST(-1, LEAST(1,
                          SIN(t.latitude * ACOS(-1) / 180) * SIN(f.latitude * ACOS(-1) / 180)
                          + COS(t.latitude * ACOS(-1) / 180) * COS(f.latitude * ACOS(-1) / 180)
                            * COS((t.longitude - f.longitude) * ACOS(-1) / 180)))) AS km
               FROM short sh
                        JOIN spare sp ON sp.product_id = sh.product_id AND sp.store_id <> sh.store_id
                        JOIN stores t ON t.store_id = sh.store_id
                        JOIN stores f ON f.store_id = sp.store_id),
     ranked AS (SELECT p.*,
                       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY to_store_id, product_id
                           ORDER BY km ASC NULLS LAST, surplus DESC, from_store_id) AS rn
                FROM pairs p)
SELECT t.store_name AS to_store, f.store_name AS from_store, r.product_id, ROUND(r.km) AS km,
       LEAST(r.need, r.surplus) AS transfer_qty
FROM ranked r
         JOIN stores t ON t.store_id = r.to_store_id
         JOIN stores f ON f.store_id = r.from_store_id
WHERE r.rn = 1
ORDER BY r.km NULLS LAST, t.store_name, r.product_id

changes._why: starting from the loss rows dropped a store with no cancellation or refund; the totals may be 0, so the divisions need a guard
request: For every store with a store-total row, show its cancelled and refunded sales, `0` where it has none, and their share of the store's sales and of the chain's, every status counted; a share is NULL where its total is `0`.
changes.sql:
SELECT st.store_name,
       COALESCE(SUM(d.total_sales), 0)                                                 AS lost_sales,
       ROUND(100 * COALESCE(SUM(d.total_sales), 0) / NULLIF(MAX(st.total_sales), 0), 1) AS pct_of_store,
       ROUND(100 * COALESCE(SUM(d.total_sales), 0) / NULLIF(MAX(g.total_sales), 0), 2)  AS pct_of_chain
FROM store_orders st
         LEFT JOIN store_orders d ON d.store_name = st.store_name
    AND d.total IS NULL
    AND d.order_status IN ('CANCELLED', 'REFUNDED')
         CROSS JOIN (SELECT total_sales FROM store_orders WHERE total = 'GRAND TOTAL') g
WHERE st.total = 'STORE TOTAL'
GROUP BY st.store_name
ORDER BY pct_of_store DESC NULLS LAST, st.store_name

changes._why: the price-only order decides which ties qualify, but leaves them in any order; an outer order by product_id, outside FETCH ... WITH TIES
request: Show the ten most expensive priced products, every product tied with the tenth included, ordered by price, the highest first, and then by `product_id`.
The order inside decides which products qualify; the one outside only orders them, so a `product_id` does not change which ties are kept.
changes.sql:
SELECT product_id, product_name, unit_price
FROM (SELECT product_id, product_name, unit_price
      FROM products
      WHERE unit_price IS NOT NULL
      ORDER BY unit_price DESC
      FETCH FIRST 10 ROWS WITH TIES)
ORDER BY unit_price DESC, product_id

changes._why: order_tms is not unique; order_id breaks the tie
request: Show all of a customer's orders, the most recent first; orders placed at the same moment are ordered by `order_id`, the highest first.
changes.sql:
SELECT order_id, order_tms, order_status, store_id
FROM orders
WHERE customer_id = :customerId
ORDER BY order_tms DESC, order_id DESC

changes._why: the recall question, answered exactly, by product_id through order_items
changes.title: Contact the customers of a recalled product
request: A supplier has recalled a product.
Customer care wants every order that included it, with the customer's name and email address, the most recent first; orders placed at the same moment are ordered by `order_id`.
changes.sql:
SELECT o.order_id, o.order_tms, c.full_name, c.email_address
FROM order_items oi
         JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
         JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE oi.product_id = :productId
ORDER BY o.order_tms DESC, o.order_id DESC

changes._why: keeps the view's Basic tier after CO_CUSTOMER_ORDER_PRODUCTS_B_01, with what the view is good at: a total and a summary of the products
changes.title: Review a customer's completed baskets
request: Customer care wants a customer's completed orders, each with its total and the summary of its products, the most recent first.
changes.sql:
SELECT order_id, order_tms, order_total, items
FROM customer_order_products
WHERE customer_id = :customerId
  AND order_status = 'COMPLETE'
ORDER BY order_tms DESC, order_id DESC

changes._why: several views group by the product's name, and the exercises take a group for a product; nothing makes the name unique
changes.title: Product names that more than one product has
request: The views group by a product's name, and the exercises on them take a group for one product; the schema does not make the name unique.
Find the names that more than one product has, with how many; the check passes when nothing comes back.
changes.sql:
SELECT product_name, COUNT(*) AS products
FROM products
GROUP BY product_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY product_name

changes._why: the order totals assume every order has lines; the foreign key holds only the other way
changes.title: Orders without a line
request: The exercises on order totals assume every order has at least one line; the foreign key holds only from the line to the order.
Find the orders with no line, the most recent first; the check passes when nothing comes back.
changes.sql:
SELECT o.order_id, o.order_tms, o.order_status, o.customer_id, o.store_id
FROM orders o
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.order_id = o.order_id)
ORDER BY o.order_tms DESC, o.order_id DESC

changes._why: nothing keeps the stock from going below 0, which the replenishment and out-of-stock exercises assume
changes.title: Negative stock
request: Nothing in the schema keeps `PRODUCT_INVENTORY` from going below `0`, which the replenishment exercises assume.
Find the inventory rows with a negative stock, the most negative first; the check passes when nothing comes back.
changes.sql:
SELECT inventory_id, store_id, product_id, product_inventory
FROM inventory
WHERE product_inventory < 0
ORDER BY product_inventory, store_id, product_id

changes._why: the image columns of PRODUCTS are read by no exercise; Claude's (missing or out of date) over Codex's (missing)
changes.title: Products missing a fresh picture
request: The web team wants the products that have no picture, or whose picture was last changed before `:since`, those that never had one first.
changes.sql:
SELECT product_id, product_name, image_filename, image_last_updated
FROM products
WHERE product_image IS NULL
   OR image_last_updated < :since
ORDER BY image_last_updated NULLS FIRST, product_name

changes._why: no exercise pages past the first rows; Oracle's OFFSET ... FETCH NEXT, and a unique tie-break
changes.title: The next page of a customer's order history
request: The account page shows a customer's orders `:pageSize` at a time, the most recent first.
Show the page that starts after the first `:offset` orders; `order_id` breaks a tie, so a page neither repeats nor skips an order.
changes.sql:
SELECT order_id, order_tms, order_status, store_id
FROM orders
WHERE customer_id = :customerId
ORDER BY order_tms DESC, order_id DESC
OFFSET :offset ROWS FETCH NEXT :pageSize ROWS ONLY

changes._why: dates are grouped but never compared across periods; LAG over an aggregate
changes.title: Month-over-month sales
request: Finance wants the revenue of completed orders per month, next to the month before and the change in per cent.
`LAG` takes the previous month that has sales, not the previous calendar month.
changes.sql:
SELECT order_month,
       revenue,
       LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_month)                                       AS previous_revenue,
       ROUND(100 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_month)) / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_month), 1) AS change_pct
FROM (SELECT TRUNC(o.order_tms, 'MM') AS order_month, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS revenue
      FROM orders o
               JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
      WHERE o.order_status = 'COMPLETE'
      GROUP BY TRUNC(o.order_tms, 'MM'))
ORDER BY order_month

changes._why: ORDER_ITEMS.SHIPMENT_ID is read only from the line's side; a shipment no line points to is the reverse
changes.title: Shipments that carry nothing
request: Before dispatch, logistics wants the shipments that no order line is assigned to, with their store, customer and status.
changes.sql:
SELECT sh.shipment_id, sh.store_id, sh.customer_id, sh.shipment_status
FROM shipments sh
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.shipment_id = sh.shipment_id)
ORDER BY sh.shipment_id

changes._why: the DDL says LINE_ITEM_ID runs from 1 within an order, but does not enforce it; the receipt relies on it
changes.title: Orders with gaps in their line numbers
request: The schema describes `LINE_ITEM_ID` as a number starting at one for each order, but does not enforce it.
Data quality wants the orders whose line numbers do not run 1, 2, 3, ... without gaps, with their number of lines and their first and last line number; the check passes when nothing comes back.
changes.sql:
SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS lines, MIN(line_item_id) AS first_line, MAX(line_item_id) AS last_line
FROM order_items
GROUP BY order_id
HAVING MIN(line_item_id) <> 1
    OR MAX(line_item_id) <> COUNT(*)
ORDER BY order_id

changes._why: the view's items is a LISTAGG, cut short, and a name matches inside another (Men's / Women's Jacket); no text match is exact. CO_SCHEMA_B_04 answers the recall by product_id; Claude had proposed padding the list with its delimiter
